annotation_description: Playing Mountain instead of Arid Mesa on turn 1 is suboptimal. Arid Mesa is a fetch land that can find a Mountain, and playing it first preserves flexibility. With Ruby Medallion in hand (wanting to cast it turn 2), playing Arid Mesa now and cracking it later (or immediately) thins the deck. More importantly, if the opponent plays something like Orcish Bowmasters, having the fetch uncracked gives you the option to fetch at instant speed in response. Playing the basic Mountain first means you'll play Arid Mesa on a later turn when you might prefer to play Commercial District or Castle Locthwain instead. Fetch lands are generally better to play early to maximize deck thinning and sequencing flexibility.

With two Castle Locthwains and two Swamps in hand, playing Castle Locthwain first is slightly suboptimal. Since Castle Locthwain enters tapped unless you control a Swamp, playing it turn 1 means it enters tapped and you have no mana available this turn. Playing a Swamp first would give you 1 black mana available on turn 1 (relevant for potential plays), and then playing Castle Locthwain on turn 2 alongside the second Swamp would let it enter untapped since you'd already control a Swamp. By leading with Castle Locthwain, you guarantee it enters tapped, and on turn 2 you'll play a Swamp (untapped), giving you only 2 mana. If you had led Swamp turn 1, then Castle Locthwain turn 2 enters untapped, also giving you 2 mana on turn 2 — the same. However, the key difference is that leading Swamp gives you 1 mana on turn 1 for potential instant-speed plays (like holding up for Orcish Bowmasters on opponent's turn 1 — though that costs 1B so you'd need 2 mana). Actually, with only 1 land either way on turn 1, you can't cast Bowmasters. But the principle of playing basics before conditional lands is correct sequencing — leading Swamp ensures Castle Locthwain enters untapped on turn 2, preserving future flexibility and tempo.

Against a Storm deck (evidenced by Desperate Ritual, Pyretic Ritual, Grapeshot, Ruby Medallion in the format), Emperor of Bones is a slow value creature that doesn't interact with the opponent's game plan. Orcish Bowmasters would be better held for the opponent's turn (it has flash) to potentially punish card draw from Wrenn's Resolve or similar effects. However, the bigger issue is that playing Emperor of Bones on turn 2 is a proactive play that doesn't pressure or disrupt a combo opponent. Holding up Orcish Bowmasters (flash) or Sheoldred's Edict mana would be more appropriate against a combo deck, keeping interaction available. That said, Emperor of Bones does apply some pressure and the opponent hasn't revealed their full game plan yet, so this is a minor sequencing/strategic error rather than a major one.

Playing Commercial District (which enters tapped) instead of Mountain wastes mana this turn. With Ruby Medallion costing 2 (reduced from nothing since it's an artifact, not red — wait, Ruby Medallion is an artifact so it costs {2}), and the hand containing Pyretic Ritual and Desperate Ritual for mana generation, having an untapped land matters. Playing Mountain would give 3 available mana (2 lands + ritual potential), enabling Ruby Medallion this turn and potentially setting up a bigger storm turn. Commercial District entering tapped means only 2 mana available from lands this turn. With Mountain, you could play Ruby Medallion (2 mana from Mountain + existing Mountain), then on future turns benefit from the cost reduction. Playing the tapped land delays the game plan by a turn.

Fetched Sacred Foundry instead of a basic Mountain, paying 2 life for no benefit. The Storm deck has no use for white mana, and the dual land type provides no advantage here since there are no future fetch lands visible.

Cast Orcish Bowmasters (a flash creature) during precombat main phase before playing their Swamp land drop. Lands should always be played before spells to maximize options. Additionally, Bowmasters has flash and could be held up for the opponent's turn to potentially punish card draw from Wrenn's Resolve or other effects, especially against a Storm opponent where disrupting their turn is valuable.

Playing a second Castle Locthwain triggers the legend rule, forcing the sacrifice of one copy. This results in only 2 lands on the battlefield instead of 3, setting them back a full turn on mana development. With Sheoldred, the Apocalypse (4 mana) in hand, reaching 4 mana quickly is critical.

Should play Mountain from hand before casting any spells to maximize available mana this turn. With 4 lands, the Storm player can chain rituals more effectively. Playing a spell before the land drop risks having less mana if the sequencing matters for the combo chain.
Casting a ritual before Ruby Medallion resolves wastes 1 mana, since the Medallion would reduce the ritual's cost from {1}{R} to {R} once it resolves.

Casting Grapeshot before Wrenn's Resolve means lower storm count and missing the chance to find additional spells (rituals, burn) from the exiled cards. Wrenn's Resolve would add +1 to storm count and potentially reveal more castable spells, significantly increasing Grapeshot's damage output.

With 0 cards in hand and opponent at 20 life, sending Grapeshot damage to face provides minimal value. Orcish Bowmasters is extremely threatening against a Storm deck since it punishes card draws and grows the Orc Army. The storm copies (likely 4+) could clear the entire board instead of dealing inconsequential face damage.

annotation_description: GPT4om Gramps cast Sheoldred's Edict during their own combat step, forcing each opponent to sacrifice a nontoken creature. However, Grok4F Coach controls NO creatures at all — their battlefield has only lands and Ruby Medallion. The Edict does literally nothing, wasting a card for zero value. Additionally, this was cast from hand during the combat step, spending 2 mana that could have been used for other plays in the second main phase (like casting Psychic Frog or holding up Orcish Bowmasters).

Orcish Bowmasters has flash and could be held to punish opponent's card draw (especially relevant against a storm-style deck running Wrenn's Resolve and other draw effects). Deploying it in postcombat main gets the ETB trigger for 1 damage but loses the option to flash it in response to opponent drawing extra cards, which could be more impactful.

Playing Arid Mesa from hand instead of one of the Wrenn's Resolve exiled cards (Bloodstained Mire or Elegant Parlor) which will expire at end of next turn. The exiled cards should be prioritized since they have a time limit, while Arid Mesa in hand can be played any future turn.

Playing Arid Mesa as the land drop when at 2 life is nearly useless - it cannot tap for mana and cracking it costs 1 life (going to 1) which is extremely dangerous against Orcish Bowmasters that can ping. The land drop is wasted on a card that provides no immediate resources.

Casting Past in Flames first uses all available mana (3 mana after cracking Arid Mesa), leaving 0 mana to flash back any rituals from graveyard. The combo chain fizzles immediately. With 2 Orcish Bowmasters and lethal on board next turn at 2 HP, this likely loses the game.

Opponent is at 1 life with no blockers. GPT4om Gramps has multiple creatures on board (Emperor of Bones, two Orcish Bowmasters, Orc Army Token) that can attack for lethal in combat, or could cast Soul Spike (exiling two black cards from hand) to deal 4 damage to the opponent. March of Wretched Sorrow can only target creatures or planeswalkers, not players, so it cannot deal lethal damage to the opponent.

GPT4om Gramps chose to let March of Wretched Sorrow target Sheoldred, the Apocalypse (their best creature, a 4/5 with deathtouch and powerful draw/life triggers) instead of a much less valuable creature. The opponent at 1 life gains X life regardless of which creature is targeted, so the X damage amount is fixed - only the creature lost matters.
